title: Do LLMs Take Care of Their Own? Similarity Signals Can Induce Cooperation
abstract: arXiv:2608.12125v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As LLM-based agents with user-instructed goals are becoming widely deployed, they increasingly encounter each other in strategic interactions, and face challenges of finding mutually beneficial outcomes. Prior literature has argued that cooperation problems such as the Prisoner's Dilemma are resolvable in settings where agents know they follow very similar decision making patterns, as for example in monocultural AI ecosystems. Following that line of work, this paper introduces the first framework for evaluating LLM decision making when agents are provided with graded similarity signals.   Among our findings, we establish that different LLM models vary drastically in how they navigate similarity signals, with some modern models showing consistent behavior across cooperation problems, payoff structures, and prompt framing. translated_title: 大语言模型会关心自己的同类吗？相似性信号可以诱导合作
translated_abstract: 摘要：随着基于大语言模型、具有用户指定目标的代理被广泛部署，它们在战略互动中越来越频繁地相遇，并面临寻找互利结果的挑战。先前文献认为，在代理知道自己遵循非常相似的决策模式的环境中，例如在单一文化的人工智能生态系统中，囚徒困境等合作问题是可以解决的。沿着这一研究方向，本文首次提出了一个框架，用于评估当代理获得分级相似性信号时的大语言模型决策制定。在我们的发现中，我们确定不同的大语言模型在如何利用相似性信号方面差异巨大，一些现代模型在合作问题、收益结构和提示框架中表现出一致的行为。也许令人惊讶的是，我们的实验还表明，计算相似性信号所基于的数据集也会影响结果。
tldr: 本文首次提出一个框架，评估大语言模型代理在分级相似性信号下的决策，发现不同模型在利用这些信号诱导合作方面表现差异显著，且相似性信号的计算数据集会影响合作行为。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the first framework for evaluating LLM decision-making under graded similarity signals, revealing significant model variations in inducing cooperation and showing that the dataset used for similarity computation influences outcomes.
